claims.claim_text: Can't Stop analysis shows four-dice odds flatten the distribution, middle columns dominate, probabilistic stopping wins, and forced moves balance design.
claims.evidence_quote: Four-dice probabilities flatten the distribution... Probabilistic strategies dominate... forced-move rule compensates for the mathematical imbalance.
claims.reasoning: Each summary component matches a conclusion in the source.

claims.claim_text: Push-your-luck rules: roll four dice, pair freely, bust loses turn progress.
claims.evidence_quote: roll four dice, pair them up however you want... if you can't move any of your three active markers, you lose everything you've gained that turn
claims.reasoning: All three rule elements are stated directly.

claims.claim_text: Board columns 2 to 12 vary 3 to 13 steps; complete three to win.
claims.evidence_quote: columns numbered 2 through 12... Columns 2 and 12: 3 steps... Column 7: 13 steps. You need to complete three columns to win.
claims.reasoning: Range and completion condition match source exactly.

claims.claim_text: Forced-move rule requires taking every legal move from the chosen pairing.
claims.evidence_quote: you must make ALL legal moves from that pairing, even if you don't want them
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of the forced-move rule.

claims.claim_text: Chasing 7 on {6,7,8} can force an unwanted 2 onto the board.
claims.evidence_quote: you're forced to take BOTH the 2 and the 7, even though column 2 isn't in your plan
claims.reasoning: Matches the source example precisely.

claims.claim_text: Four-dice pairing flattens the probability distribution versus two dice.
claims.evidence_quote: Four-dice probabilities flatten the distribution
claims.reasoning: Source conclusion states this explicitly.

claims.claim_text: Two-dice baseline: 7 hits 16.67%, six times more likely than 2.
claims.evidence_quote: sum 7 is the most likely at 16.67%, and it's exactly 6x more likely than sum 2 at 2.78%
claims.reasoning: Numbers match exactly.

claims.claim_text: Four dice yield exactly three possible pairings per roll.
claims.evidence_quote: That's it, just three possible pairings.
claims.reasoning: Count of three pairings is stated in source.

claims.claim_text: Making a 2 needs two 1s: 171/1296, about 13.2%.
claims.evidence_quote: P(can make a 2) = ... = 171/1296 approx 13.2%
claims.reasoning: Fraction and percentage match the source.

claims.claim_text: Making a 7 via inclusion-exclusion: 834/1296, about 64.4%.
claims.reasoning: Fraction and percentage match the source.

claims.claim_text: Probability ratio 4.88 nearly matches length ratio 4.33; designers thought carefully.
claims.evidence_quote: The probability ratio from 2 to 7 is 4.88. The length ratio is 4.33. Pretty close! The game designers were definitely thinking about this.
claims.reasoning: Both ratios and the inference match the source.

claims.claim_text: Column combinations matter more than individual column odds.
claims.evidence_quote: Column combinations matter more than individual columns
claims.reasoning: Source conclusion states this directly.

claims.claim_text: Expected rolls cluster near 20; long column 7 completes slightly faster than 2.
claims.evidence_quote: For column 2: 3/0.132 = 22.73 rolls. For column 7: 13/0.644 = 20.18 rolls. Column 7 is slightly faster
claims.reasoning: Values and comparison match the source.

claims.claim_text: {6,7,8} succeeds 92% per roll; {2,3,12} only 43.8%.
claims.evidence_quote: {6,7,8}, you have a 92% chance of not busting... {2,3,12}: 568/1296 = 43.8% success rate
claims.reasoning: Both success rates match the source.

claims.claim_text: 37 combos rate excellent; median succeeds 79.6%, worst collapse to 43.8%.
claims.evidence_quote: 37 combinations are 'excellent'... median combination still succeeds 79.6%... worst combinations drop dramatically to just 43.8%
claims.reasoning: All three numbers match the source.

claims.claim_text: Stopping rule weighs expected gain against bust-weighted unsaved progress.
claims.evidence_quote: Keep rolling if: (P_success x Q) > (P_bust x U)
claims.reasoning: Describes the source heuristic formula accurately.

claims.claim_text: Roll on {6,7,8} with five steps banked; stop on {2,3,12} with two.
claims.evidence_quote: On {6,7,8} with 5 unsaved steps... keep rolling. On {2,3,12} with 2 unsaved steps... STOP.
claims.reasoning: Both step counts and decisions match the source.

claims.claim_text: Only 39.8% of {6,7,8} rolls are clean; {2,3,12} just 2.3%.
claims.evidence_quote: Only 39.8% of rolls give a clean move on {6,7,8}... For {2,3,12}: Only 2.3% of rolls are clean!
claims.reasoning: Both percentages match the source.

claims.claim_text: Continuing current columns usually beats switching, but author hedges: switching unanalyzed quantitatively.
claims.evidence_quote: The mathematics favor continuation in most cases... I haven't fully analyzed this aspect quantitatively.
claims.reasoning: Hedge is preserved exactly as in source.

claims.claim_text: 3.6M-game simulations crown probabilistic, consistent strategies over fast ones.
claims.evidence_quote: 3.6 million total games... Probabilistic strategies dominate the top rankings... consistency beats raw speed
claims.reasoning: Combines source findings faithfully.

claims.claim_text: 38 strategy families tested across single-player and head-to-head simulations.
claims.evidence_quote: I tested 38 strategies across 14 different strategic families
claims.reasoning: Number 38 is right for strategies, but source reports 14 families, not 38, mislabeling the count.

claims.claim_text: GreedyUntil1Col fastest at 10.5 turns but busts 7.5 times per game.
claims.evidence_quote: GreedyUntil1Col is fastest (10.5 turns)... bust rate (7.5 per game)
claims.reasoning: Both figures match the source.

claims.claim_text: FiftyPercentSurvival wins 69.84% by stopping below 50% cumulative survival.
claims.evidence_quote: FiftyPercentSurvival dominates with 69.84% overall win rate... Roll until cumulative survival probability drops below 50%
claims.reasoning: Win rate and rule match the source.

claims.claim_text: Consistency beats raw speed; pure greedy loses nearly everything.
claims.evidence_quote: Consistency > Speed... The pure Greedy strategy (never stop voluntarily) lost essentially every game.
claims.reasoning: Both claims are stated in the source.

claims.claim_text: First player wins 55.59%, an 11.18% edge exceeding chess and Go.
claims.evidence_quote: Player 1 wins 55.59%... First-player advantage: +11.18%... larger than chess (~5%) or Go (~7%)
claims.reasoning: All figures and comparison match the source.

claims.claim_text: Board is nearly balanced singly; forced moves compensate combination imbalance.
claims.evidence_quote: The deviations are +-13.6% at most... forced-move rule compensates for the mathematical imbalance
claims.reasoning: Both components are stated in the source.

claims.claim_text: Single-column completion deviates at most 13.6% from 20 rolls.
claims.evidence_quote: The deviations are +-13.6% at most.
claims.reasoning: Deviation bound matches the source.

claims.claim_text: Adding one step per middle column would quadruple balance precision.
claims.evidence_quote: Optimal board (+-1 step from current)... 4x more balanced with just +1 step!
claims.reasoning: The 4x improvement and +1 step match the source.

claims.claim_text: Forced moves contaminate strong combos, keeping strategy choices interesting.
claims.evidence_quote: add rules that turn that imbalance into interesting strategic choices
claims.reasoning: Source describes forced moves as contamination and a balancing mechanism.

claims.claim_text: Play middle columns consistently; designers should favor playability over perfection.
claims.evidence_quote: Aim for columns 5-9... prioritize consistency over aggressive play. For game designers: Prioritize playability over mathematical perfection
claims.reasoning: Both recommendations restate the source.

claims.claim_text: Aim for columns 5-9, avoid edge columns, prioritize consistency over aggression.
claims.evidence_quote: Aim for columns 5-9, avoid forcing activation of columns 2-3 and 11-12, and prioritize consistency over aggressive play
claims.reasoning: Advice matches the source exactly.

claims.claim_text: All code, simulations, and datasets are published for reuse.
claims.evidence_quote: All analysis code and simulation results are available
claims.reasoning: Source states code and results are available.
